story.summaryZh: 诺里斯在圣保罗大奖赛雨战中夺冠后表示，迈凯伦在2027赛季前仍需努力，目前还“没有达到争夺世界冠军的水准”。

story.originalTitle: Norris: McLaren still not at championship level
story.summaryEn: Lando Norris said after winning the rain-affected Sao Paulo Grand Prix that McLaren still have work to do ahead of 2027 and are "not at the level to fight for a world championship."
detailZh: 诺里斯表示，尽管在圣保罗大奖赛夺冠，迈凯伦在2027赛季仍没有达到争夺世界冠军的水准
诺里斯在受降雨影响的圣保罗大奖赛中领先近15秒夺冠，但他认为迈凯伦在2027赛季前仍需努力，才能再次争夺世界冠军；拉斯维加斯大奖赛各节练习与排位将于11月20日至22日在天空体育F1直播
克雷格·斯莱特对雨中的圣保罗大奖赛作出点评：诺里斯夺冠，维斯塔潘从后方追赶，梅赛德斯锁定车队总冠军
诺里斯认为，尽管自己在圣保罗大奖赛混合条件下以压倒性优势夺冠，迈凯伦“仍未达到争夺世界冠军的水准”。
诺里斯本赛季第三次将杆位转化为胜利，迈凯伦在巴西带来的升级（包括新翼片和底板部件）立即带来了性能提升。
但诺里斯觉得自己受益于对手的失误，包括领跑比赛时打滑的安东内利，以及在维修区打滑的拉塞尔，这扩大了他对红牛车手马克斯·维斯塔潘15秒的获胜优势。

他说：“我们本周末带来的升级很棒。它们发挥了应有的作用，所以如果我们没带来这些升级，我们会落后更多。就这么简单。但这仍然不够。”
“这些还不足以让你突然之间总是最快。我认为在像周日这样的日子里，并不全是关于这个。关键在于好的策略、好的进站、开得好并且不犯错。”
“我确实有一辆可以让我争夺胜利的赛车，这非常重要。那些事情会有帮助。很难量化它帮助了多少，但升级总是有帮助的，而且它们效果很好。所以，车队做得非常出色。”
兰多·诺里斯赢得圣保罗大奖赛，红牛车队的马克斯·维斯塔潘和伊萨克·哈贾尔分列其后
诺里斯的胜利是迈凯伦自八月荷兰大奖赛以来的首场胜利，尽管他们在九月的马德里西班牙大奖赛上因不合时宜的虚拟安全车而未能获胜，颇为遗憾。
他说：“尽管我们很高兴能够带来一些东西并向前迈进一步，还拿到了杆位和一场胜利，但我们并没有达到本可以有的那么高兴，因为我们也知道自己还不够好。”
2026年圣保罗大奖赛精彩集锦
“我们还没有达到所需的水平。我们目前对现有的整体套件还没有信心。我们正在慢慢接近目标。我们想更快做到，但这很困难。”
“我们知道我们还有工作要做，我们还没有达到争夺世界冠军所需的水平。所以，我为车队正在做的工作感到骄傲，但我们都知道我们还有工作要做。”
斯特拉：诺里斯在最佳状态下是F1最好的车手之一
诺里斯承认，周日他在巴西的表现是自2019年进入F1以来最好的胜利之一。
迈凯伦车队领队安德烈亚·斯特拉表示，诺里斯驾驶得“非常出色”，并且“处于最佳状态”。
他补充道：“当兰多发挥出最佳水平时，他绝对是赛道上最优秀的车手之一。”
兰多·诺里斯表示，在他的圣保罗大奖赛胜利中，车队在正确的时间换上正确的轮胎方面做得非常出色。
“我们已经在这样的条件下看到了这一点，比如在排位赛中，这已经不是第一次了，当你面对混合多变的条件下，他算是最快找到极限的车手之一。
“你在正赛中也看到了这一点，当时赛道处于干湿之间。那正是他在比赛中可能比任何人都收获最多的时候。
兰多·诺里斯在赢得圣保罗大奖赛后，在领奖台上打碎香槟瓶的新角度画面
"他对可用抓地力的感知非常敏锐，而且我要说，作为一名车手他甚至相当全面，尽管从技术角度看，在理解如何运用自己的工具来利用可用抓地力、或适应赛车平衡方面，他前面还有很多年——因为你永远不会有真正完美的赛车。
"你永远不会有完美的条件，所以适应能力实际上可能是你作为车手最想具备的最重要特质。当需要理解什么是最好的、如何操作时，他绝对是一位大师。"

detailEn: Lando Norris says McLaren are still not at the level to fight for world championship in 2027 despite Sao Paulo Grand Prix win

Lando Norris won a rain-affected Sao Paulo Grand Prix by nearly 15 seconds but he feels McLaren still have work to do ahead of 2027 to fight for the world title again; watch every session of the Las Vegas Grand Prix from November 20-22, live on Sky Sports F1
Craig Slater gives his verdict on a wet Sao Paulo GP, where Lando Norris won, Max Verstappen fought from the back and Mercedes secured the constructors' title
Lando Norris believes McLaren are "not at the level to fight for a world championship" despite his dominant win in mixed conditions at the Sao Paulo Grand Prix.
Norris converted pole position into victory for the third time this season as McLaren's upgrades in Brazil, including new wings and floor components, gave them immediate performance.

But, Norris feels he benefitted from mistakes, including Kimi Antonelli who spun when leading the race, and George Russell who spun in the pit lane, which exacerbated his 15-second winning margin over Red Bull's Max Verstappen.

"The upgrades we brought this weekend were great. They worked as they should have done, so if we didn't bring them, we'd be further behind. Simple as that. But it's still not enough," he said.
"They're not enough to say you're suddenly always the quickest. I think on a day like Sunday, it's not all about that. It's about good strategy, good pit stops, driving well and not making mistakes.

"I certainly had a car that I could fight for a win with, and that's very important. Those things would help. It's hard to quantify how much it's helped, but upgrades always do, and they worked well. So, the team has done a very good job."
Lando Norris wins the Sao Paulo GP ahead of Red Bull's Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar
Norris' triumph was McLaren's first since August's Dutch Grand Prix, although they were unfortunate to now win September's Spanish Grand Prix in Madrid following an untimely Virtual Safety Car.

"As much as we're happy we've managed to bring things and take a step forward, and come away with a pole and a win, we're not as happy as we could be because we also know we're not good enough," he said.
Highlights from the 2026 Sao Paulo Grand Prix
"We're not at the level we need to be. We're not confident in the package we have just yet. We're getting there slowly. We want to do it quicker, but that's difficult.

"We know we still have work to do, and we're not at the level we need to be to fight for a world championship just yet. So, I'm proud of the team for the work they're doing, but we all know that we still have work to do."
Stella: Norris one of the best drivers in F1 when at his best
Norris admits his performance in Brazil on Sunday was "up there" among his best victories in F1 since joining the sport in 2019.
McLaren team principal Andrea Stella says Norris drove "brilliantly" and was "at the top of his game".
"When Lando operates at his best, he's definitely one of the best drivers on the grid," he added.
Lando Norris says his team did a very good job getting on the right tyre at the right time during his Sao Paulo GP win
"We have seen that in these conditions, like in qualifying, it's not the first time that when you have mixed variable conditions, he kind of is one of the fastest in finding the limit.
"And you have seen this in the race as well, when the track was in the middle between dry and wet. It was when he was probably gaining most throughout the races on anybody else.
New angles of Lando Norris shattering his champagne bottle on the podium after winning the Sao Paulo Grand Prix

"He's very sensitive in understanding how much grip is available and very, I would say, even complete as a driver, despite he still [has] many years ahead of him, from a technical point of view, in terms of understanding how to deploy his tools to use the grip that is available, or to adapt to the balance of the car, because you're never going to have a really perfect car.

"You're never going to have the perfect conditions, so adaptability is actually probably the most important feature that you may want to possess as a driver. When there's a need to understand what's best, how to operate, he's definitely a master."

detailEn: Qatar GP Qualifying: George Russell bounces back with superb performance to beat Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position

George Russell beats Kimi Antonelli to pole as Mercedes seal dominant one-two; Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri on second row; Isack Hadjar beats Max Verstappen to fifth; watch the Qatar Grand Prix live on Sky Sports F1 at 4pm on Sunday, with build-up from 2.30pm
George Russell took pole position in Qatar as Kimi Antonelli seemed unhappy with his lap during qualifying
George Russell produced a superb performance in Qatar Grand Prix Qualifying to beat his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli to pole position.

The reignition of Russell's feud with Max Verstappen at last weekend's Las Vegas Grand Prix had dominated the build-up to the penultimate race of the season, but the Brit produced the perfect response as he topped all three parts of qualifying.

That came as a surprise after Antonelli, who sealed the drivers' title with four rounds to spare, had topped all three practice sessions, but the Italian was unable to match Russell when it mattered most.

McLaren found significant improvement on the final runs to move ahead of Red Bull as Mercedes' nearest challenger and lock out the second row, with Lando Norris ahead of Oscar Piastri as the best of the rest despite being marginally either side of half a second down on Russell.
Verstappen, who said after winning in Las Vegas last weekend that Russell is "far below" his level, was beaten to fifth by his Red Bull team-mate Isack Hadjar.
Charles Leclerc took seventh but his Ferrari team-mate Lewis Hamilton was beaten to eighth by Racing Bulls' Arvid Lindblad, with the latter's team-mate Liam Lawson completing the top ten.

George Russell says Lewis Hamilton is an equally 'ruthless competitor' to Max Verstappen but that his former team-mate has 'incredible values, grace and dignity'. Watch the full interview during Sky Sports F1's live Qatar GP coverage on Sunday
Kimi Antonelli outpaced Mercedes team-mate George Russell in final practice for the Qatar Grand Prix as the Silver Arrows continued to dominate.

Antonelli, who topped both of Friday's practice sessions, outpaced Russell by 0.249s and it looks highly likely a Mercedes driver will be on pole position after qualifying, which takes place later on Saturday at 6pm (build-up from 5.15pm), live on Sky Sports F1.
Mercedes appear to have a half-second advantage over the rest field as Max Verstappen was 0.510s adrift of Antonelli and the other Red Bull of Isack Hadjar was 0.687s behind.

Mercedes' dominance is a surprise as nearly every race following August's summer break has been very competitive at the front but it seems a combination of the smooth, high-speed track layout and Mercedes finally getting on top of their upgrades from a month ago has given them a significant margin on their rivals.
"Mercedes are almost in a class of their own, so it's worth the rest looking at the gap to Verstappen [in third]," said Sky Sports F1's Bernie Collins.

Ferrari had a difficult Friday after a spin for Charles Leclerc and an engine issue for Lewis Hamilton, but Leclerc fared better in final practice in fifth, ahead of McLaren's Lando Norris and Oscar Piastri.
Hamilton was unhappy throughout the session and stated his "car won't turn" after his final flying lap which put him in ninth, in between Racing Bulls duo Arvid Lindblad and Liam Lawson.
